patients.summary: Woman in her thirties with morbid obesity who joins in 2023; routine labs find a high calcium that becomes primary hyperparathyroidism, treated with cinacalcet she later drops, then a localized left parathyroid adenoma removed in January 2026 with normal calcium since.

events.reason: New patient, establish care and physical

conditions.label: Severe obesity due to excess calories

social.value: Less than one drink per week

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
31F joining us from her previous primary care office, which she left because the wait for appointments had gotten long. Feels well. No specific complaints today.

PMH: obesity, long-standing. Has tried calorie tracking apps on and off; weight has hovered in the same range for several years. No prior surgeries. No medications, no supplements.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family: mother treated for an underactive thyroid. Father has passed kidney stones several times. A maternal aunt had a parathyroid problem, patient unsure of details.
Social: works as an administrative data specialist, desk job. Never smoked. Alcohol rarely, well under a drink a week. No drugs. Lives on her own in Westfield.

ROS: negative in full, including no fatigue, bone pain, urinary symptoms or GI change.

Exam: BMI 43. Well-appearing. Thyroid without nodules or enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, obese. Extremities without edema. Skin without acanthosis. Mood and affect normal.
PHQ-2 = 0.

Assessment/Plan:
1. Preventive care. Baseline CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, TSH (family history). One-time HIV and hep C screening, she agrees. Pap was done at her old office in 2021, will confirm with records, next due 2026.
2. Severe obesity, BMI 43. Talked through realistic targets, protein-forward meals, a walking routine she can do after work. She'd like to start with these changes. Revisit at follow-up.
3. Records release signed for the prior office.
Vaccines: flu and COVID when the fall supply arrives.
Follow up in about 6 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Beth, thanks for coming in. Almost everything looks good: blood counts, cholesterol, sugar (A1c), thyroid and kidney function are all normal, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens are negative.

The one thing I'd like to keep an eye on is your calcium, 10.7, just a touch over the upper limit. Often that's a one-time blip. We'll repeat it when I see you this winter. Nothing you need to change in the meantime, just keep drinking water normally.

Take care.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Received by fax after a second request: 14 pages from the patient's previous primary care office, covering visits 2018 through early 2023.

Contents: annual visit notes, immunization record, Pap smear report 2021 (negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy, HPV negative). Problem list on their end shows obesity only. No medications listed. No lab panels within the past two years were included.

Filed to media. Flagged to PCP.

documents.title: Outside records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed prior office records. Nothing that changes the plan. Pap 2021 normal with negative HPV, co-test due 2026. No old calcium values to compare against, unfortunately.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here after work for vaccines. Afebrile, no current illness, no prior vaccine reactions. Flu vaccine given L deltoid, COVID booster R deltoid. VIS provided. Observed 15 minutes, no reaction. Left ambulatory.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Six-month follow-up. Weight about the same. Has been walking at lunch a few days a week, less since the cold weather. Eating pattern unchanged, says the evenings are the hard part. No new symptoms; specifically denies fatigue, thirst, urinating more than usual, constipation, aches or kidney stone pain. No calcium or vitamin D supplements, no antacids.

O: Vitals per flowsheet. BMI 43. Comfortable. Neck without palpable mass. Heart and lungs normal. No edema.

A/P:
- Calcium was 10.7 in August. Repeating today along with intact PTH, vitamin D and phosphorus. With her aunt's parathyroid history I want to know where the PTH sits.
- Severe obesity: discussed again. She'd like to keep working on it on her own for now. Offered nutrition visit, she'll think about it.
Will call with results.

documents.title: Lab results call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt with results. Calcium 10.9, higher than August. Intact PTH 96, above range, which it shouldn't be with a high calcium. Vitamin D 31, adequate. Kidney function normal.

Explained this pattern points to primary hyperparathyroidism, most often from one overactive parathyroid gland. Reassured that it is common and usually slow. Referral to endocrinology placed; she prefers an office closer to work. Pt verbalized understanding. Encouraged good hydration in the meantime, no calcium supplements.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with food

documents.title: Update from endocrinology
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, just wanted to let you know I saw the endocrinologist on Friday. They said surgery isn't the best idea for me right now because of my weight and started me on a pill called cinacalcet, 30 mg twice a day. I have to get blood work in two weeks. Not sure if they send you anything so figured I'd tell you.

documents.title: RE: Update from endocrinology
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thank you for letting us know, Beth. I've added cinacalcet to your medication list as prescribed by endocrinology. We haven't received their note yet and will request it. Take it with food, and reach out if you notice nausea or tingling around your mouth.

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation, date of service 2024-04-19
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOCRINE PRACTICE
New consultation. Date of service: 04/19/2024
Reason for referral: hypercalcemia with elevated PTH

History: 32-year-old woman sent by her primary care physician after routine chemistry showed mild hypercalcemia on more than one occasion, with intact PTH above the reference range on the most recent draw. She has no complaints. No history of nephrolithiasis or fracture. No lithium or thiazide exposure.

Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: maternal aunt with primary hyperparathyroidism; father with repeated kidney stones; mother hypothyroid.
Social: never smoker, drinks very little, office work in data administration.

Exam: BMI 43. Alert, in no distress. No palpable neck mass. Cardiopulmonary exam normal. No proximal weakness.

Impression: primary hyperparathyroidism, mild, presently asymptomatic.
Given her body habitus (BMI 43), we consider her a poor surgical candidate at this time and will treat medically.

Plan:
- Start cinacalcet 30 mg by mouth twice daily with meals.
- Serum calcium two weeks after starting.
- Return in six months.

Addendum 05/06/2024: calcium drawn 05/03/2024, two weeks on cinacalcet, is 10.1 mg/dL. Continue current dose.

cc: primary care

documents.title: Outside records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Endocrinology consult from April finally here, after our second request. Cinacalcet 30 BID, calcium down to 10.1 at two weeks. Med list already reflects it. Referral closed.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. Sorry to have missed her in August, she had a deadline at work.

Interval: seen by endocrinology in April for primary hyperparathyroidism, on cinacalcet 30 mg twice daily since. Taking it with breakfast and dinner, no stomach upset. Their two-week calcium was 10.1. Due back with them this fall; she hasn't scheduled yet.
Otherwise feels well. Sleeping fine, energy fine. No urinary or bowel changes.

Meds: cinacalcet 30 mg BID. NKDA.

Exam: BMI 43. Pleasant, well. HEENT normal. Neck supple, no mass. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, obese, nontender. No edema. Skin unremarkable.
PHQ-9: 2.

A/P:
1. Health maintenance: CMP, CBC, lipid panel today. Tdap (last one over 10 years ago per old records), flu and COVID given. Pap due 2026.
2. Primary hyperparathyroidism on cinacalcet: calcium today; reminded her to book the endocrinology follow-up.
3. Severe obesity: stable weight. Still prefers lifestyle approach. We set a goal of three 30-minute walks a week.
RTC one year.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Beth, your labs from Tuesday are fine. Calcium 10.2, better than the 10.9 before cinacalcet and close to normal. Cholesterol, blood counts and kidney function all normal. Please do get that endocrinology follow-up on the calendar.
